clue.text: It's an advance in transport and protection

parts.note: a van is a vehicle for transporting goods
a guard gives protection

explanation.surface: A news item about a breakthrough in vehicle safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'in' and 'and' are link words; the vanguard is the advance party at the front of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: The front part of a moving army, its leading body, is also called its advance guard.

clue.text: Substantiate in the light provided

indicators.note: the word for provided goes inside the flare's name

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol
provided means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: Confirm a claim in the light of the evidence supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the light' looks like a phrase, but 'the light' is a Very light, a signal flare, with IF placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To substantiate is to confirm with evidence, to check and prove true.

clue.text: Not quite noble in New York

indicators.note: the nobleman's title is set inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who almost made it in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost is another way of saying not quite, falling just short.

clue.text: Being located in a particular place, buy tie to suit

definitions.text: Being located in a particular place

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged to fit what is needed, as clothes are altered to suit

explanation.surface: A shopper picking a necktie to match a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suit' rearranges BUY and TIE. Ubiety is a rare philosophical word for whereness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubiety is a rare word for the state of having a definite position, whereness.

clue.text: Tries a much different a remedy for sufferers

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Tries a much different a remedy for sufferers', gives the anagram TRIES A MUCH, but no clue words define RHEUMATICS and the stray 'a' suggests garble; no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Tries a much different a remedy for sufferers

clue.text: Work that's a drag to engage in

parts.note: to wage war is to engage in it, so the phrase gives the verb meaning carry on

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a tedious job they must take on.
explanation.definitionFit: Towage is the job of hauling a vessel by rope, literally dragging it along.

clue.text: Prevail over firm I object to

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
me is the object form of I

explanation.surface: Someone protesting against a company winning out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' is not a protest but grammar: ME is the object case of I. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To win through in the end, beating difficulties, is to triumph.

clue.text: A coir mat of subtle pervasive quality

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A coir mat of subtle pervasive quality', has the fodder A COIR MAT and a definition (Chambers: aroma, any subtle pervasive quality) but no anagram indicator; a word may be missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: A coir mat of subtle pervasive quality

clue.text: They go beyond the limit of moderation

definitions.text: They go beyond the limit of moderation

parts.words: They go beyond the limit of moderation
parts.note: describes things that overstep what is reasonable, overindulgences

explanation.definitionFit: Overindulgences are acts that pass the bounds of temperance.

clue.text: Made capital out of one leader's move

indicators.note: a move changes position, so these letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone profited from a political leader's manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges I (one) with LEADERS, the possessive's S counting as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into cash, turning it into capital.

clue.text: Describes a great figure who is in charge

parts.note: a hero is a great, admired figure

explanation.surface: A description of a great leader who runs things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who is' is a link; the definition treats the answer as a describing word, an adjective applied to a great figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective is a word that describes, and this one is applied to the brave and grand.

clue.text: Replete at the end of 90 minutes?

definitions.text: Replete at the end of 90 minutes?

parts.words: Replete at the end of 90 minutes?
parts.note: a football match lasts 90 minutes; the clue reads its final whistle as a time of being stuffed full

explanation.definitionFit: The final whistle of a football match after ninety minutes is called by this phrase, whose first word also means sated.

clue.text: In seconds a record-breaking athlete commonly gets away fast

indicators.note: the athlete's name is set in between the two letters for seconds

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second, so two of them give SS
Steve Cram, the British middle-distance runner, set world records in the 1980s

explanation.surface: A star runner sprints off within seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a British runner who held world records at 1500m and the mile; 'commonly' marks the definition as slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a slangy order to clear off quickly, so the word means leaves in a hurry.

clue.text: Put in type of dwelling for a printer?

definitions.text: Put in type of dwelling for a printer?

parts.words: Put in type of dwelling for a printer?
parts.note: a printer sets up type, so a home for a printer might be one he sets up; the phrase really means to establish a home

explanation.definitionFit: To establish a household is to start living in one's own home.

clue.text: Redesign the flow of a watercourse

definitions.meaning: to make something smoother and more efficient, reshaping how it runs
a line traced by a stream, the course of running water

explanation.surface: An engineer reshaping the channel of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplifying a process reshapes its flow, and a stream's course is a line of running water.

clue.text: They take a stand against work some stand for

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
posers are people who pose, standing for a painter or photographer

explanation.surface: Protesters resisting a work some people support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand for' looks like support but means pose for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are against something resist or contest it.

clue.text: Given rope Charles Lamb discovers an offspring of Lear

parts.note: a cord is a thin rope
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: An essayist, handed a rope, comes upon a character from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' and 'discovers' are links. Charles Lamb wrote 'Essays of Elia'; he also retold Shakespeare's plays, King Lear among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordelia is the youngest of King Lear's three daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Injured, having hurried out of a shower maybe

indicators.note: the word for hurried stands outside the word for the shower

parts.note: sped means hurried
a shower is one example of rain

explanation.surface: Someone twisted an ankle dashing out of the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' puts SPED outside RAIN; the shower is weather, not the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprained joint is one hurt by wrenching its ligaments.

clue.text: The outlook to us is circular

parts.note: a prospect is an outlook or view ahead

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark that the future just goes round in circles for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'is' are links; 'circular' is a noun here, a printed leaflet, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A brochure sent out to advertise a school or share issue is a kind of printed handout.

clue.text: Recruit about 21

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a different order

parts.note: refers to the answer at 21 down, meaning marine arms

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking for a recruit around another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of the answer to 21 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit is to sign up or join, as soldiers do.

clue.text: Domain of politician in the Irish republic

indicators.note: the politician is placed inside the republic's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: The territory of an Irish politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by one power is its dominion or territory.

clue.text: Marine arms, silent sort

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Quiet types serving in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' are not weapons but arms of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow bays and creeks reaching into the land are arms of the sea.

clue.text: Pass as the chimney-pot, say

definitions.meaning: out of date, no longer in fashion
a chimney-pot was a nickname for the tall silk top hat, an old-fashioned piece of headgear

explanation.surface: A remark that a style has gone out like the tall top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' on the page lost its accent: it is 'Passé'. A 'chimney-pot hat' was the Victorian tall silk hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of fashion is outdated, and a Victorian topper is literally an aged piece of headgear.

clue.text: Oriental spinner?

parts.note: in cricket a left-arm bowler's unorthodox spinning delivery has a dated name built from an Eastern man

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a left-arm wrist-spinner's delivery that turns into the right-hander is given this old name; the clue reads it as a spinning man from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket names a left-arm unorthodox spin ball with this dated term for a man from the Far East.

clue.text: Genial sort of place in Len don

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so these letters are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A friendly sort of neighbourhood in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GENIAL. Ealing is a district of west London, home of the famous film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is a borough in the west of the English capital, known for its film studios.

clue.text: Disciplinary to a notably soft single group I've joined

parts.note: in musical notation p (piano) means soft
a unit is a single group, one complete body
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone describing a strict musical ensemble they have joined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notably' points to musical notes: p, piano, is the marking for playing softly. 'to a' and 'joined' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishing measure is one meant to correct or discipline.

clue.text: Needing and swallowed a drink

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, as a mouth takes in food

parts.note: shy can mean lacking or short of, as in two players shy of a team

explanation.surface: Someone thirsty gulped down a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing' is a stretch for shy, used as in 'a pound shy of the price'. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer, a light pub beverage.

clue.text: Uneasy with the others to a smaller extent

parts.note: the rest are the others, the remainder
less means to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: Someone feeling uncomfortable among the group, though not as much as before.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to relax or keep still is a kind of unease.
